summary: Notes from an early network meeting. Topics included revisions to the contractor's IMP-host specification, revisions to RFC 11, and the transmission of multiple control messages. It records the discussion and is not a protocol document.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 21 records topics from an ARPANET meeting held at UCLA on 10 October 1969. Participants discussed changes to the IMP-host memo, revisions to RFC 11 and sending multiple control messages.

questions: what did the october 1969 arpanet meeting discuss
subtitle: Notes on topics discussed at an October 1969 ARPANET meeting.

tldr.problem: ARPANET participants needed to discuss proposed changes and clarifications to network documents.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 21 records topics from a meeting at UCLA: changes to BBN Memo 1822, revisions to RFC 11 and transmission of multiple control messages.
tldr.outcome: The note records discussion points and information about proposed revisions; it is not a complete protocol specification.

today: The unit metadata records RFC 21 as Unknown and lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. Its text is a meeting record dated 17 October 1969.

sections.title: Meeting Topics and Participants
sections.content:
The note says a network meeting was held at UCLA on 10 October. Participants came from SDC, UCLA and UCSB.

The listed topics were revisions to BBN Memo 1822, revisions to NWG/RFC 11 and transmission of multiple control messages.
sections.plainLanguage: People from three ARPANET sites met to discuss network documents and control messages. RFC 21 records the main topics, not a full transcript.

sections.title: Changes to BBN Memo 1822
sections.content:
The note reports that an IMP could handle up to 63 active transmit links and 63 active receive links. If a new transmit link was requested when 63 were already active, the IMP would send a Link Table Full message and discard the message.

It also records a rule that an unused link entry would be deleted after 26 seconds. Cerf asks whether deletion should happen only when the transmit table is full; Crocker responds that otherwise entries could accumulate. The note also clarifies that message type 6 was unassigned and that the type written as 10 was octal, meaning type 8; types 9-15 were unassigned.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo changes set limits for active links and remove entries after a period of disuse. The meeting note also clarifies which message type numbers were assigned.

sections.title: Revisions to RFC 11
sections.content: The note says RFC 11 had been overtaken by developments at UCLA and discussions with other network nodes. It identifies RFC 22 as containing some of the major changes and says an updated version of RFC 11 was forthcoming.
sections.plainLanguage: The participants noted that work had moved beyond RFC 11. The note points to RFC 22 for some major changes and says a revised version was expected.

sections.title: Multiple Control Messages
sections.content:
The final topic is transmission of multiple control messages. The note says George Gregg of UCSB would publish RFC 23 on sending multiple control messages over control links.

RFC 21 reports this planned work but does not define the message format or transmission procedure itself.
sections.plainLanguage: The meeting raised the topic of sending several control messages over control links. A separate RFC was planned to address it.
